about: About Founded in 1975, Dublin Business School specialises in the provision of career-focused education. The school has evolved over the years, expanding their offerings to meet the demand of various sectors. The extensive suite of programs include: business, finance, law, computing, media, arts, psychology and social science. DBS works closely with industry and professional bodies to ensure quality and relevance of material, and employability of graduates, to drive meaningful and impactful careers. Why Dublin Business School? Location : Dublin Business School is truly in the heart of Dublin city, a mere two minute walk from St. Stephens Green, the Laus and all main bus routes. The educational sites in the prime city centre locations of Aungier street and George's street are within a few minutes walking distance of each other and provide students with access to all of the infrastructure capabilities of a vibrant modern capital city. Internationally Recognised Education Experience : Over the last 47 years, Dublin Business School has established a considerable international reputation for the quality of programmes. This recognition has been achieved both at government level and on an individual student basis. Dublin Business School has created a unique learning environment with students from over 70 countries participating in its programmes. Commitment to World Class Teaching : As an institution, Dublin Business School focuses their main research activity on the constant improvement of the learning experience of their students. Also, all of their programmes have been designed and developed in collaboration with industry and the professional bodies so that on graduation in addition to their academic qualifications, students will have the skills and knowledge for a successful career. Student Centred Approach : At Dublin Business School, they take a holistic view of college life. Academia should be integrated with a stimulating social scene. The work/study balance is something that Dublin Business School regards as being important. Accordingly they organise, through their dedicated student services department, a range of social, sports and developmental activities for students. Show More

about: About On a limestone bluff overlooking the River Lee in Ireland is University College Cork (UCC). Its motto ‘Where Finbarr Taught, Let Munster Learn,’ refers to the 6th century Saint Finbarr, whose monastery and school once stood nearby. Originally named Queen’s College, Cork, the university was established to provide access to higher education in the Irish province of Munster (Ireland's second city), and was named after Queen Victoria, along with two other Queen’s Colleges in Galway and Belfast. UCC's first students arrived in 1849 and, from 1850, the institution formed part of the Queen's University of Ireland. In the 1880s it became part of the Royal University of Ireland, and by 1908 joined the federal National University of Ireland (NUI), where it was a founding member. The landscaped gardens and surrounds of UCC are known as ‘the quad’ and superstition holds that students crossing the quad before graduation risk bad luck and failure in exams. Alongside the quad, the university is centred around its Aula Maxima – the Great Hall, which acts as the ceremonial and symbolic heart of the university. The Hall's design, inspired by the great universities of the Middle Ages, was the work of renowned Irish architects Thomas Deane and Benjamin Woodward. Since 1908, UCC has grown exponentially, offering a research-led curriculum across 120 degree programmes in Humanities, Business, Law, Architecture, Science, Medicine and more. With a student body of some 20,000, including 3,000 international students, UCC returned to being a university in its own right again in 1997, retaining its original name. UCC’s alumni includes the prominent mathematician Professor George Boole, who most famously invented Boolean logic, as well as the feminist and politician, Mary MacSwiney. Among UCC’s many historical collections and artefacts are the ancient Ogam stones, thought to be the earliest written source of the Irish language. Why University College Cork: Location : Cork is the largest and southernmost county of Ireland. It is a place of great wit, culture and independence. Cork City is a hub of culture and business whilst the county boasts some of the country's most magnificent landscapes. It is the perfect place to live, learn and thrive! Research : University College Cork (UCC) is an internationally competitive, research-led university that plays a key role in the development of Ireland’s knowledge-based economy. Our institutional research strategy focuses on creating and supporting world-leading clusters of researchers, building on the research strengths of the University. Student Life : Student life in UCC is great and students can get involved in many ways: Students’ Union, the Mardyke Sports Arena, Clubs and Societies (there are over 100 to choose from)Cork City (theatre, music, art, food culture, festivals), and Cork County (beaches, history, scenery). about: About Maynooth University is an internationally recognised institution located 25 kilometres outside of Dublin, Ireland, and is the nation’s fastest growing university. One of four constituent universities of the National University of Ireland, Maynooth University in 2021 placed #88 in the global top 100 universities under 50 years old in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings. Today, Maynooth University is a place of lively contrasts–a modern institution, dynamic, rapidly-growing, research-led and engaged, yet grounded in historic academic strengths and scholarly traditions. Maynooth’s unique collegial culture fosters an interdisciplinary approach to research, which its world-class academics bring to bear in tackling some of the most fundamental challenges facing society today. The University’s research institutes and centres consolidate and deliver this impact as vibrant communities of learning, discovery and creation. Research at Maynooth also is very much central to its teaching, and the University prides itself on placing equal value on its research and teaching missions. Why Maynooth University: World-Class Education : In addition to being named in the Times Higher Education's Top 100 Under 50, Maynooth University is recognised among the top 350 universities in the world, the top 200 European universities, and as one of the top 200 universities for international connections and outlook. International Community and Opportunities : With over a third of academic staff coming from abroad and many academics and graduates working internationally, Maynooth University has built up a wealth of global connections. This means that students at Maynooth benefit from an international outlook, and those who wish to study abroad for a semester or an academic year during your degree have a network of connections to tap in to. During the course of their academic degree students from Maynooth have studied subjects such as Law at Boston College, Mandarin Chinese at Beijing Foreign Studies University and Music in the University of Vienna. Location : Situated just 25 kilometres west of Dublin city centre, and well serviced by bus and rail routes, Maynooth is Ireland's only university town. Located close to the Irish and European headquarters of many multinational high tech companies, the university continues to forge strong links with industry and is well placed to cater for the growing demand for high quality graduates. Student Life : Maynooth University has a reputation for being a particularly sociable university - a recent poll of 10,000 third level students voted Maynooth Ireland's friendliest college. Along with the Students’ Union, there are over 100 clubs and societies on campus, providing the lifeblood of student activity. From Archery to the Tea Society, whether students are seeking adventure, fitness, relaxation or fun, there is an active student life waiting. Show More

about: About University of Limerick (UL) is a young, energetic and enterprising university with a proud record of innovation in education and excellence in research and scholarship. The university offers more than 70 undergraduate programs and 100 taught postgraduate programs. Each year, students come to University of Limerick from more than 100 countries in pursuit of a world-class education in business, science and engineering, sports, health sciences, arts, and social sciences. T he triple-accredited Kemmy Business School places UL amongst the world's top 1% of business schools. T he university's facilities give students opportunities to gain hands-on experience in simulated settings like the Wall Street-stule Trading Floor, flight simulator, moot court, patient simulation suites, and state-of-the art digital labs. Located on 148 hectares in the west coast of Ireland, along the picturesque River Shannon, UL is ranked in the the Top 20 green campuses in the world . S tudents study in a safe and supportive environment and this has contributed to UL's being voted number one in the world for student experience. Why University of Limerick Campus : Voted #1 in Ireland for clubs and societies, UL has over 80 student-run groups, as well as volunteer opportunities that allow them to explore their interests while making new friends and familiarizing themselves with student life in Ireland. Location : Located 30 minutes from Shannon International Airport, Limerick is Ireland's 3rd largest city and one of the most affordable for student living. Many global companies are based here and the city offers students a great selection of cultural and recreational options as they explore life in Ireland! Global rankings leader : UL has ranked 16th in the world for Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions (Times Higher Education Impact Rankings, 2021), Top 75 in Europe for Excellence in Teaching and Learning (THE - Teacher Ranking, 2020), and QS 5 Star Rating (2021). International student support : Voted the best international support in Ireland, UL offers a full suite of support options to newcomers, ranging from 5 Learning Centres in writing, language, math, science and IT, to counselling and wellbeing services. Internship Opportunities : UL has partnered with 1,700 industry-leading employers including Deloitte, Stryker, Boeing and Intel. Internships allow students the chance to develop practical working skills during their studies which significantly improves their employment prospects. Show More

about: About Dublin City University is proud to be on of the world's leading Young Universities, with a mission to transform lives and societies. Since its inception, Dublin City University has worked to support learners all over Ireland. Entrepreneurial, innovative, and creative, Dublin City University has been listed as 1st in Ireland, and 23rd in the world for graduate employability. The University is always seeking to innovate in teaching, exploring new technologies, and providing flexible pathways to university level education. Students in their academic journey will be supported with world-class facilities, as well as research and study spaces such as libraries. Aside from academics, Dublin City University also has a thriving and diverse student culture, welcoming students from over 122 countries. Apart from sports clubs, there are over 100 student societies to choose from. Dublin City University believes in welcoming diverse groups of students from all walks of life. The first in Ireland, in 2016, Dublin City University became a University of Sanctuary. The University works to build a culture of hospitality for people seeking sanctuary. This includes offering educational scholarships to those seeking refuge in Ireland. Why Dublin City University? High Employment Rate : 96% of recent grads are in employment or further education six months after graduation Work Placement: 80% of programs have INTRA - paid relevant work experience or work placement 128 Different Nationalities - DCU attracts students from around the globe DCU is #1 in Ireland: DCU is ranked #1 in Ireland for graduate employment rate Show More
